---
title: "Matching Methods for Multilevel Data in Education Research"
subtitle: "A practical guide and illustration of approaches in R"
---

**SREE 2026 workshop** · Baltimore, September 2026 · 2 hours

**Instructors:** Jordan Rickles (UCLA) and Alberto Guzman-Alvarez (American Institutes for Research)

This site holds the hands-on materials for the workshop. Each page is the R code from one chapter of the handbook *Propensity Score Matching in Multilevel Educational Settings*, with the explanatory text removed so the code can be run top to bottom. The data and package setup in Chapter 4 is shown from the handbook, which is linked in the top bar.

## Before the workshop

Install R, RStudio or Positron, download this repository, run the install script, then run the setup check. The full list of what to bring and have installed is on the [Before you come](before_you_come.qmd) page.

## The documents

| Document | Handbook chapter | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| [MIAD](05_miad.qmd) | 5 | Students assigned to treatment within schools. Seven propensity score models, four matching approaches, balance at the site level, individual-average and site-average effects, FIRC, sensitivity analysis. This is the page we run together in the room. It ends with a "Try it" block and an own-data template. |
| [Decision flowcharts](flowcharts.qmd) | 3 | The guiding questions and options at each stage for the MIAD and CAD, for use with your own study |
| [CAD](06_cad.qmd) | 6 | Whole schools assigned to treatment. Cluster-level propensity score, cluster-global, sequential, and network-flow matching, two-level balance, cluster-average and individual-average effects, permutation inference, sensitivity analysis |
| [MCAD](07_mcad.qmd) | 7 | Teachers assigned to treatment within schools, with students nested in teachers. This design combines the other two. It is not covered in the session and is included for reference. |

Each document follows the same six stages. Define the estimand, define the distance measure, implement the matching method, assess the matched sample, analyze outcomes, and run a sensitivity analysis.

## The data

All examples use `data/timss_df.rds`, which is TIMSS 2015 Grade 4 mathematics for Canada, 2,478 students nested in teachers nested in schools. The three treatment indicators were constructed from observed covariates to illustrate the three designs. They are not real interventions, and the estimates in these documents are illustrations of the workflow, not findings. See `data/README.md` for the variable list and caveats.

## Using the code with your own data

The chunks are written so that the dataset, the treatment indicator, the site identifier, and the covariate formulas are set near the top of each stage. Replace those objects with your own to run the workflow on your study. Your data needs one row per individual with a 0/1 treatment column, a site or cluster identifier, the covariates, and the outcome. The "Your own data" block at the end of the Chapter 5 page lists the five objects to change.
